summary: Ramez Naam (quoted as saying it on August 4 on the Moonshots podcast) and Dave Blundin argued that NVIDIA's CUDA software moat is eroding: Naam said 'The CUDA moat is broken this year and next,' because a frontier model can now recompile AI code to run fast on an AMD chip; Blundin said he has been writing custom kernels for Fable 5 himself over recent weeks, work that used to require a team of specialists but is now done with a prompt, and concluded that CUDA as an inference-time moat is 'already dead' and as a training-time moat has a 'limited lifespan,' with ninety to ninety-five percent of the AI workload moving to inference. quote: Now listen to Ramez Naam, who said on August 4: “The CUDA moat is broken this year and next.” Why? Dave confirmed he’s been writing custom kernels for Fable 5 himself over the last few weeks. Work that used to require a team of specialists is now done with a prompt. … Dave’s conclusion: CUDA as an inference-time moat is already dead. As a training-time moat, limited lifespan. Ninety to ninety-five percent of the AI workload is moving to inference.
